title: Phase 2: Docs and Files You Can Trust
eyebrow: Design for approval · roadmap phase 2 (#494) · nothing built yet

short.lead: Before another account can pick up where a session stopped (phase 3), the record of where it stopped has to be right. This phase makes every session end with the docs agreeing with the code and a changelog line for what changed. Merged branches and finished helper copies are cleaned up once their work is safe on GitHub, and no big generated files reach git. I checked the 17 old issues this phase carries against the code on 2026-11-11. Five are already built and only need proof, and the other 12 are covered by the changes below. One part needs your PC: why PlunderSpell's folders take over 153 GB.

items: Not measured: that folder is on your PC, and this cloud session was refused access to the PlunderSpell repo. The likeliest cause is helper copies (git worktrees) that are never removed: this session alone made 6 of them in this repo. Each is a full checkout, and in a Unity project each copy can also grow its own Library folder of generated files. The new disk report (choice 4) measures it on your PC at the next session start, with no command for you to run.

changes: new
Docs that disagree with the code are caught when the code changes
Drift is caught at the commit that causes it (choice 1).

Docs in this repo cite code as file:line (for example design_loop.py:1322) and by file path. Today nothing checks those citations after the code moves. docref.py checks only the archivist's doc-ref pointers, and the commit reminder only asks whether some doc was staged.
The commit reminder in the guard hook asks only whether any docs/ file was staged.
The reminder names each doc that cites a changed file, and a drift check flags citations to files or lines that no longer exist.
A wrong doc is named in the commit that made it wrong, so it can't sit unnoticed.
new
A changelog in every repo
Each repo keeps CHANGELOG.md, and every change adds a plain line to it (issues #384 to #388 and #244; choice 2).

The plugin ships a changelog template. The session-start docs check (the docstiers hook) names a repo that has none. Opening a pull request whose branch leaves the changelog unchanged gets a reminder. The documentation rule names the changelog. Lines lead with plain words ("adds 2 rules"), then the exact detail ("+14 lines in the rules file"), as you asked in #244.
No repo has a changelog; what changed is only in commit messages.
CHANGELOG.md, scaffolded with the docs tiers, with an Unreleased section each change adds to.
You can read what changed in a repo without reading commits.
new
Merged branches and finished copies are cleaned up
Local branches and helper worktrees go once their work is safe on GitHub (#156; choice 3).

A local branch is deleted only when everything on it is in a merged pull request and pushed. A helper worktree (a separate working copy of the repo that a helper builds in) is removed only when it is clean and its commits are on a pushed branch. Nothing with unsaved work is ever deleted; the guard's existing rules still apply. Remote branches are left to GitHub's own "delete branch after merge" setting.
The worktreesweep hook only commits work a killed helper left behind.
After a merge, the merged branch and its finished worktrees are deleted, and the session says which.
Your disk and branch list stop filling with finished work.
new
Big generated files never reach git, and disk use is visible
A commit that adds a large or generated file is refused, and session start reports where the disk went (choice 4).

The guard refuses a commit that adds a file over a size limit, with a starting value of 50 MB to be tuned. It also refuses a file inside a folder a game engine or build regenerates (Unity's Library/, Temp/, obj/, Builds/, node_modules/) when .gitignore does not cover it. Each refusal names the .gitignore line to add. Session start reports the size of each helper worktree and generated folder when they pass a starting threshold of 5 GB.
Nothing stops a generated folder being committed, and nothing reports disk use.
The commit is refused with the fix named, and session start names the big folders.
PlunderSpell's 153 GB is explained on your PC, and the cause can't grow back unnoticed.
new
Three rules from old issues
Never hardcode tunable values (#117), a session finishes its own task (#301), and no rule ships without a check (#228; choice 5).

#117: values a person may want to change go in a settings file or an exposed field, not in code, unless they were set by measurement. #301: work for another repo becomes an issue in that repo, and the session returns to its own task. #228: a verify.py case fails when a rule in rules/house-rules.md names no check that enforces it.
The rules say nothing about hardcoding or switching tasks, and some rules have no check.
Two rule lines, each with a check, and a test that every rule names its check.
A rule the agent could quietly skip can no longer be written.
new
A place for research, sources and vocabulary
A research log and a vocabulary list beside the decisions log (#336, #45).

docs/6-decisions/ gains Research.md (what was researched, with sources cited) and Vocabulary.md (the project's terms and the reversals that settled them). The docs-tier check names them as optional, not required.
Research and settled terms live in chat or nowhere.
Two files beside Decisions.md, scaffolded with the docs tiers.
A later session can find why something was decided and what a word means.
keep
Already built: five old issues
Five old issues, #199, #399, #404, #479 and #463, are already in the code; each gets a verify.py case so it can close with proof.

#199: the branch rule ("Off main: commit, push, merge freely") is in rules/house-rules.md. #399 and #404: docs/4-systems/work-tracking.md says built, and the rclink hook is in docs/architecture.md. #479: folder deletes git can undo, "Continue from" and "Issues for" are in safe_git.py and design_loop.py. #463: finished by phase 1.
choices: q1
Where is a doc that disagrees with the code caught?
A
At the commit that changes the code: the reminder names each doc citing a changed file, and a citation to a missing file or line is flagged
Caught where it happens, by the session that knows why the code changed.
B
Only by a check you or a session runs on request
Nothing new at commit time, but drift waits until someone looks.
A matches "drift is caught where it happens" in the phase's goal; B leaves the gap that let docs drift.
q2
What does a changelog line come from?
A
The session writes it, and the end-of-turn check sends the turn back once if files changed but no changelog line was added
Written while the work is fresh, never skipped (#244's "done automatically").
B
Only a reminder when a pull request opens
Less noise per turn, but lines are written later from memory.
A is what #244 asked for; the end-of-turn check already exists, so this only extends it.
q3
What happens to a merged branch and its finished helper copies?
A
Deleted locally once everything on them is merged and pushed; the session says which
No action from you, and nothing unsaved can go.
B
Listed at session start; deleted only when you say so
You see every deletion first, but it is one more thing for you to answer.
A keeps your hands free; the safety rule (merged and pushed, nothing uncommitted) is what protects the work.
q4
What happens when a big or generated file is about to be committed?
A
The commit is refused and the .gitignore line to add is named
The file never reaches GitHub, where removing it later means rewriting history.
B
A warning only; the commit goes through
Never blocks, but one missed warning puts gigabytes on GitHub.
A: once a big file is pushed it is expensive to remove, so stopping it first is the cheap fix.
q5
Which of the three rule changes go in this phase?
A
All three: no hardcoding, a session finishes its own task, and every rule names its check
The phase closes all 17 of its issues.
B
Only "every rule names its check" now; the other two wait for a later phase
A smaller phase, but #117 and #301 stay open.
A: each rule is a short text change plus one check, and the check rule makes the other two enforceable.

wrapup.summary: The design for phase 2: docs agree with the code, every repo has a changelog, finished branches and copies are cleaned up, and big files never reach git.
